title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure | WIRED
body:
# A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure

Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. [...] Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind's Signal evaluation. But even this analysis was limited in scope—it did not, for example, formally verify the entire Signal mobile app—and DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one [...] The researchers say that some of their crucial advancements are in developing a “human-AI collaboration process,” as Chaudhuri puts it, that allows agents to contribute and self-correct at almost every phase of the process while still seeking human input and review at key junctures. “We don’t want this sort of vibe world where AI is generating the goals and AI is generating the proofs and basically taking tests that are self-written," Chaudhuri says. “There’s a middle ground.”

Nvidia remains the leading AI infrastructure company, as its graphics processing units (GPUs) are still the primary chips used to power AI workloads. While Nvidia dominates much of the AI chip market, large hyperscalers are increasingly turning to custom AI accelerators to help reduce costs, especially when it comes to inference.
